::: {#rem-process-notation}

#### Subscripts and parentheses for a stochastic process

The notation for a [stochastic process](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/notation.html#def-stochastic-process)
uses both slots at once.
A stochastic process is an [indexed family](sets.qmd#def-indexed-family) of [random variables](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-random-variable) $X_t$,
one for each index $t$ in some [index set](sets.qmd#def-index-set), such as time.
The index goes in the subscript, because it picks a member of the family.
Each $X_t$ is itself a [function](functions.qmd#def-function) of the [outcome](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-experiment-outcome) $\omega$ of a [random experiment](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-random-experiment),
that is, an element of the [sample space](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-sample-space),
so the outcome goes in the parentheses: $X_t(\omega)$.
Fixing $\omega$ and letting $t$ vary traces out one path of the process.
Many sources drop $\omega$ and write $X_t$, or write $X(t)$ when $t$ is continuous.

:::
